registerPolicy: 해요체 in every learner line, all ten paths, including friend paths. By explicit policy 반말 never appears in any of the four turns, so the sentence-final 반말 ban runs on interlocutor lines too. Interlocutors (staff, colleagues, neighbors, friends) also speak 해요체; the fixed chunks 안녕하세요/죄송합니다/감사합니다/알겠습니다 are the only 습니다 forms in any turn (decided: no further 습니다 in staff openings). Honorific direction has two separate mechanisms: (1) humble verbs 드리다/말씀드리다/부탁드리다 lower the learner as actor toward a respected recipient, so the learner is the correct grammatical subject: 내일 다시 연락 드릴게요, 서류를 드렸어요, 확인 부탁드려요, 제가 보내 드릴게요. (2) subject-honorific -(으)시- raises its grammatical subject, so in learner lines it appears only with the other person as subject (언제 오세요?, 확인해 주시겠어요?, 시간이 되시면) and never with the learner as subject (no 제가 가세요, no 제가 연락 드리세요). -아/어 주시겠어요?/주시면 안 될까요?/주세요 ask the respected interlocutor to act; -아/어 드릴게요 offers the learner's own action. Staff may use -(으)시- toward the learner (손님, 내일 오시면 연락 주세요). Learner never asserts a decision only staff can make (refund granted, visit date fixed); learner asks, staff decides, learner accepts with modification.
genderSafety: Korean verbs, adjectives and past forms carry no speaker gender, so no agreement hazards. By authoring choice, not as a claim about adult native usage (언니/형/오빠 are normal between intimates), the lessons stay role-neutral: no gender-marked address or role terms in any of the four turns (오빠/언니/누나/형/아저씨/아줌마); use 선배, 동료분, 이웃분, 선생님, 사장님, 직원분, 기사님. Kinship referents inside narration (어머니, 할머니 in P8 L5/L10) are allowed; they are referents, not address. Captions describe roles (die Kollegin/the colleague acceptable in base text only; target text stays role-neutral). Validator check is exact-token: after edge punctuation stripping, an eojeol equals a banned term or banned term + 아/야/는/은/이/가/도/한테/들; never a substring regex, so 형 inside 형태/인형/유형/모형 is not flagged. No gendered recall, trophy or required speech tokens are possible.
orthography: Standard Hangul with 표준어 spacing (것 같아요, 수 있어요, 못 해요 spaced; 안 돼요 spaced; -고 나서 spaced). Prices and dates Arabic digits plus Sino-Korean reading context (3만 원, 15일, 7시 반 digits allowed as in A2); small counts native numeral plus counter (두 개, 세 번). Loanwords in 외래어 표기법 spelling. Captions quote the opening in base text with German „…“ and English “…” exactly as A2. Target punctuation: . ? , only; no ellipses, no emoji, no romaji.

segmentation.youOne: First learner reply: 6-12 eojeol, one or two sentences, ends in 요-form or 요-question; contains trophy surface and the three speech tokens.
segmentation.youTwo: Second learner reply (continuation/resolution): 5-9 eojeol, one sentence, carries the 2-3 cloze blanks and resolves or modifies.
segmentation.chunks: 4-7 chunks; each chunk one meaningful eojeol group (1-3 eojeol) that joins with single ASCII spaces to exactly the first reply string; never split inside an eojeol; endings stay attached to their stem.
segmentation.speechTokens: Three distinct whole lexical eojeol taken verbatim from the first reply after stripping edge punctuation .?, from each eojeol (가능할까요 from 가능할까요?, never the token with ?); tokens contain Hangul/digits only, suffixes included (왔는데, 가능할까요, 연락); choose content eojeol, never 네/저/그/좀; optional tokens cover the rest; matching is whole-eojeol against the punctuation-stripped reply, no substring, stem or suffix tolerance.
segmentation.trophyAnchoring: Trophy is the canonical dictionary form (adverb or noun). The lesson declares the exact reviewed surface eojeol in which it occurs in the first reply and in its example (e.g. canonical 가능, surface 가능할까요; canonical 예전, surface 예전에는; canonical 갑자기, surface 갑자기). Validator checks that the declared surface eojeol is present verbatim and that surface minus canonical is empty or in the reviewed per-lesson remainder list (particles 이/가/을/를/은/는/에/에서/에는/도/로/으로/만/까지/부터, copula 예요/이에요, 하다-inflections for 하다-nouns). No automatic substring search: 강 inside 강남 or 일 inside 일정 must fail. Prefer natural bare surfaces (adverbs, noun compounds like 신청 방법, colloquial object omission like 연락 드릴게요); particles are never dropped merely to make the surface bare.
segmentation.acceptedInput: Only explicit reviewed variant rows: documented spacing/contraction pairs (것 같아요 / 거 같아요), 저는/전, 그것은/그건, and digit vs Hangul numeral for the same number. Variant matching compares whole eojeol after edge punctuation stripping on both sides, so punctuation-only differences (수 있을까요 / 수 있을까요?) need no variant row. No blanket word dropping, no automatic particle tolerance, no substring/stem guessing, no semantic substitutions. Threshold 0.65 and the existing B1 recording window of 15 s stay unchanged; A2's 12 s is historical evidence, not a B1 requirement.

knownTraps: -는데 (background) vs -아/어서 (cause) and 때문에 (noun cause): staff and review must check the German base does not force weil onto a background clause.
-(으)ㄹ 때 (time) vs -(으)면 (condition): German wenn covers both; English base disambiguates with when/if.

-(으)려고 (해요): authoring scope for B1 learner lines is first-person intention only (저는 5킬로를 뛰려고 해요); the language itself allows third-person -(으)려고 해요 when the speaker has evidence of that intention (동료분이 이사하려고 해요), so interlocutor lines may use it. Announced third-person plans in learner lines use -(으)ㄹ 거예요/예정이에요.
Relative-clause tense: -는 (present verb), -(으)ㄴ (past verb or adjective), -(으)ㄹ (future), -던 (recalled/incomplete); 어제 간 카페 not 어제 가는 카페.
Indirect questions: -는지 after verbs, -(으)ㄴ지 after adjectives, (이)ㄴ지 after nouns, -(으)ㄹ지 for uncertain future; 언제인지 not 언제는지.
안 vs 못: inability in P3/P9 refusals needs 못.
-고 있어요 (progressive) vs -아/어 있어요 (resultant state): 문이 열려 있어요 not 열고 있어요.
Topic/subject switch inside narration: 저는 ... 그런데 버스가 ... keep 이/가 for newly introduced actors.

Honorific direction pair: learner offering own action uses humble 드리다 with the learner as subject (내일 다시 연락 드릴게요); learner asking the other person uses -(으)시-/주시- with that person as subject (내일 다시 연락 주시겠어요?). Wrong in learner lines: 제가 연락 드리세요 (imperative aimed at self) and 제가 내일 오세요 (-(으)시- on self). Correct staff line: 내일 오시면 연락 주세요.
Spacing traps: 것 같아요, 수 있어요, 한 지, 할 수밖에, 못 해요; -곤 했어요 attaches to the stem.
Double past -았/었었어요 only for states no longer true; not a generic strong past.
Trophy false substrings: 일/일정, 강/강남, 차/차이, 방/방학; validator requires declared surface eojeol.

Base-text rendering of -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요: choose by context among German scheint/wohl/wahrscheinlich/ich glaube/ich denke and English seems/I think/probably; all mark uncertain assessment and are acceptable when they hedge accurately. Ban only mechanical calques that shift meaning (a flat ich denke, dass where the Korean reports a sensory impression, or ich glaube where the Korean asserts a known fact).
Caption must quote only the opening; openings must not leak the complication of turn three.
mechanicalValidationRules: Exactly 10 paths, ids korean-b1-* , 10 lessons each; all 100 trophies unique under NFC+casefold against each other and the full A1+A2 trophy list.
dialogue is tuple4 them/learner/them/learner, every targetText non-empty, every baseText has both de and en.

First reply 6-12 eojeol; second reply 5-9 eojeol; opening and follow-up 4-10 eojeol; eojeol counted by splitting on single spaces with punctuation left attached (가능할까요? is one eojeol); chunk reconstruction keeps punctuation verbatim.
chunks length 4-7, joined by one ASCII space equals dialogue[1].targetText exactly; terms 6-8 entries, each with de and en.

speakRequired has 3 distinct entries, each equal to a whole eojeol of dialogue[1].targetText after edge punctuation .?, is stripped from that eojeol; entries contain Hangul/digits only; none in the banned address list.

Cloze: 2-3 blanks, each kind form|connector|choice, exactly 4 choices, exactly one equals answer; form blanks carry cue (string only, German + English form label); connector and choice blanks carry no cue; every answer is a whole inflected lexical eojeol or a 1-3 eojeol phrase usable on its own, never a bare particle, pronoun, bound morpheme, bare stem or bare 것/분/곳; concatenated parts equal dialogue[3].targetText.
Recall before+answer+after equals dialogue[1].targetText; answer is one content eojeol; fallbackChoices 4 distinct including answer.
Pattern 2-3 examples; highlight is a contiguous substring of its targetText; at least one example equals dialogue[1] or dialogue[3] targetText.

trophyWord.word equals the lesson trophy; declared surface eojeol equals a whole eojeol (edge punctuation stripped) of dialogue[1].targetText and of trophyWord.example; surface minus canonical is empty or in the reviewed remainder list; no substring search.

Regex bans: sentence-final 반말 endings (어./아./야./지?/니?/자. without 요) on all four turns by explicit policy, -십시오, -습니다 except the four fixed chunks, romaji letters in targetText. Address-term check is exact-token per genderSafety, never substring. Honorific-direction checks (no -(으)시- with learner subject) run on learner turns only; staff -(으)시- toward the learner is expected.
pedagogicalGoal is a German string; situation and sceneCaption carry de and en; caption contains dialogue[0].targetText verbatim inside quotes.

Grammar-range gate: per-path staged forms may appear in learner turns only from their productive lesson range onward, or anywhere once an earlier path has made them productive; recognition-only forms appear in interlocutor turns only; P9/P10 learner turns use only families already productive in P1-P8.
semanticReviewRules: Particle correctness (이/가, 을/를, 은/는, 에/에서, 에게/께) checked line by line; colloquial omission allowed only where a native speaker would drop it in speech.
Each follow-up (turn three) adds new information or a real counter-offer; it may not restate the opening.
Learner never states what staff decide; acceptance in C paths always modifies something (time, size, quantity, method).
Cloze distractors must be either ungrammatical in slot or clearly wrong in context; no near-synonym also fits; recall distractors likewise.
German and English bases read as native speech, not glosses; concessive and background clauses rendered idiomatically.
Register coherence per lesson: same interlocutor relationship across all four turns; friend paths stay warm but 요-form.
Trophy meaning taught is the sense used in the line; whyThisWord explains reuse value in both bases.
Numbers, times and prices realistic for Korea in 2026.
Recycled A2 vocabulary may appear freely in text; only trophies are uniqueness-gated.
requiredSchemaExtensions: trophyWord.surface (optional reviewed extension): {core: string, example: string} explicit surface eojeol for the first reply and the example; validator matches whole eojeol after edge punctuation stripping, no substring heuristics.
trophyWord.remainder (optional reviewed extension): string list of allowed surface-minus-canonical remainders for this lesson (particles/copula/하다-inflection); absent or empty means exact bare form.

acceptedPhraseVariants (optional reviewed extension): explicit alternative first-reply strings per lesson (spacing/contraction/numeral), no generated variants, matched whole-eojeol after edge punctuation stripping.

Cloze stays {kind, answer, cue?: string, choices[4]}: form blanks carry a cue string like 'Hintergrund -는데 / background -는데'; connector and choice blanks carry no cue; answers are whole inflected eojeol or 1-3 eojeol phrases.
Dialogue stays the existing tuple4 with roles fixed by index (them/you/them/you); no role field is added.
Validator config, not lesson schema: the ko-KR language validator config sets its length unit to eojeol so the shared range checks count eojeol instead of Latin words.
Speech config for B1 keeps the existing values (threshold 0.65, 15 s window) unchanged; an optional pilot flag may log durations, no numeric change before measured data.

staging.productive: -(으)ㄹ 예정이에요 (P7 L9-10) + full year story and plans, only P1-P8 families

paths.clozeSchema: form blank on recalled or plan ending with cue, connector blank 그래서/그리고/그런데/그래도, choice blank on season or month
paths.recycles: all P1-P9 families, A2 future and seasons

lessons.beat: Colleague asks best memory this year; spring trip taken; asks where.
Friend compares with last year; hard job then, easier now; asks how.
Partner asks favorite season; autumn hike you took; asks for photos.
Colleague asks winter plans; studying Korean while working; asks which class.
Mentor asks lessons learned; presenting while nervous; asks for tips.
Friend asks changes; started cooking while living alone; asks signature dish.
Partner asks challenges; decided to try the exam; asks when.
Colleague asks volunteering; rewarding though tiring, decided to continue; asks frequency.
Friend asks plans; next month moving, already planned; asks if help needed.
Colleague asks new year wishes; trip and health planned; asks which first.
